systems.name: Gamma Cephei

systems.name: Rigel

systems.name: eps Ind
systems.note: Census B/C are resolved Ba/Bb. Existing MSC-generated component IDs are aliases of those same two brown dwarfs, not additional objects.

(2000), Table 3: absolute Johnson V 15.39 +/- 0.07; A/C light separation is approximate. Gonzalez-Payo et al. (2026), Table 4: M5.5V; colons mark estimated subtypes. Torres et al. (2010), Table 5: approximate bolometric log10(L/Lsun)=-3.11, marked uncertain (:); no numerical error published. No secure individual temperature, radius, age or metallicity adopted. (2000), Table 2, gives the shared EZ Aquarii ABC systemic radial velocity V0 = -50.08 +/- 0.01 km/s. The uncertainty is the published orbital-fit uncertainty on V0. Frozen J2000 positions are retained.

stars.name: Izar A
stars.notes: Reviewed Izar component: Baines et al. 2025 Tables 6-7 supersedes the heterogeneous older temperature/radius/luminosity. Radius scales as distance and luminosity as distance squared from source parallax 13.83 mas to the shared Hipparcos distance. Temperature 4341 +/-39 K is distance independent; source radius +1.30/-1.39 Rsun and luminosity 459 Lsun are retained verbatim. Shared parallax uncertainty is correlated across distance-scaled quantities; the printed 0.1 Lsun source error is not a complete luminosity error. Published seismic mass 5.36 +/-0.48 Msun (Rudrasingam 2026) retains its original 4755 K /37.61 Rsun assumptions and scaling systematics; it is not a dynamical mass or recalculated here. Preferred approximate common system distance. A is saturated in Gaia DR3 (RUWE 3.529), B has no DR3 parallax, D is faint (parallax 15.7305 +/-0.6077 mas). Hipparcos 16.10 +/-0.66 mas is compatible with D. Common-distance geometry preserves measured sky directions; unknown relative depths are set to zero, not measured to be zero. This is not an orbital solution. A and B use one compiled-primary RV bulk-motion approximation; orbital velocities are not modeled.
